nodes.text: RNA-seq Differential Transcript Usage (rnaseqDTU). Bioc Workflow `rnaseqDTU` analog: quantify transcripts (Salmon), import via tximport, then + DEXSeq + stageR for differential transcript usage with FDR control.

Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .

Assign CRISPR guide RNAs to single cells from Perturb-seq sequencing data according to Replogle et al. 2022 | CRISPR guide assignment and cell barcode demultiplexing from single-cell CRISPR screen data → single-cell AnnData with assigned sgRNA targets and non-targeting controls

Perform hit calling to identify perturbations with significant transcriptional phenotypes relative to non-targeting controls | perturbation hit calling and differential expression testing comparing target-perturbed single cells against non-targeting controls → hit significance table and target effect sizes

Learn perturbation state embeddings using scVI and scANVI deep generative modeling | deep generative perturbation embedding and latent state representation using scVI and scANVI on single-cell perturbation expression profiles → low-dimensional latent space and perturbation clusters

Germline variant calling and clinical annotation from patient whole-exome sequencing (WES) data | germline variant calling and clinical annotation from whole-exome sequencing FASTQ/BAM → annotated VCF with pathogenicity predictions

RNA-seq analysis for aberrant gene expression and aberrant splicing detection in rare disease | detection of aberrant gene expression and aberrant splicing events from bulk RNA-seq data in rare disease → expression and splicing outlier calls

Multimodal integration of annotated WES candidate variants with RNA-seq aberrant expression and splicing evidence | integration of annotated WES variants with RNA-seq expression and splicing outliers → prioritized candidate causal variants and diagnostic summary
Run RNA-seq analysis and differential expression

BioMate: Subworkflow Sprint 3 — Pseudotime + RNA velocity from single-cell data Runs two orthogonal trajectory methods in parallel: — graph-based pseudotime (R / Monocle3) — RNA velocity (Python / scVelo) Both processes accept the same AnnData h5ad input but are. 2-step pipeline: → . Inputs: csv, h5ad. Outputs: anndata, csv, h5ad, png. Key parameters: adata_h5ad, monocle_cluster, root_cell, velocity_mode.

IDAT → Normalisation → Differential Methylation → Gene Enrichment. EPIC/450K array methylation from IDAT — minfi load + functional normalisation, DSS differential methylation, missMethyl gene-set enrichment. Use when you want the DSS-based differential-methylation + enrichment wrapper chain. Also applicable to bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq.

Identify tumor-reactive T cells and clonotypes from scRNA-seq data | phenotypic characterization and identification of tumor-reactive T cell subsets from single-cell RNA-seq and TCR-seq data using activation/exhaustion gene signatures (e.g., CD39, CD103, CXCL13) → annotated reactive T cell clusters and clonal lineages

Predict tumor neoantigens and HLA binding affinities | somatic mutation-derived neoepitope prediction, patient HLA allele typing, and peptide-MHC binding affinity scoring → prioritized candidate neoantigens

Nanostring GeoMx DSP Analysis (GeoMxWorkflows). Bioc Workflow `GeoMxWorkflows` analog: read Nanostring GeoMx DSP NanoStringGeoMxSet, segment-level QC, Q3 normalization, mixed-model linear DE across regions of interest.
predict CYP450 inhibition and hepatic clearance for new chemical entity

Illumina 450k/EPIC Methylation Array DMR Analysis (methylationArrayAnalysis). Bioc Workflow `methylationArrayAnalysis` analog: read IDAT files via minfi, QC, normalize (SWAN or noob), call DMPs (limma), DMRs (DMRcate), gene-set test (missMethyl).
FDA Phase II to Phase III dose justification brief
RNA-seq differential expression analysis to derive a transcriptional signature | bulk RNA-seq differential gene expression analysis → ranked differentially expressed gene signature

Query transcriptional signature against drug perturbation libraries (e.g. LINCS L1000 / Connectivity Map) to identify matching compounds | transcriptomic connectivity mapping against perturbagen signatures (LINCS L1000 / CMAP) → prioritized list of matching drugs
test compound effect over time at 0, 6, 24, and 72 hours
Run Voyager spatial ESDA on this Visium dataset

Public RNA-seq Reanalysis (recountWorkflow). Bioc Workflow `recountWorkflow` analog: pull uniformly-processed counts from recount2/3 for a study (e.g., SRP), scale counts by read length, run DESeq2 DE with technical replicate handling.

Estimate human PK parameters from preclinical animal data (rat, mouse, dog) using interspecies allometric scaling | interspecies allometric scaling of preclinical pharmacokinetic parameters (clearance, volume of distribution) to project human PK values

Full mechanistic PBPK simulation with compartmental organ model, organ-specific clearance, and renal/hepatic impairment submodels | physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulation with organ clearance and special population (renal/hepatic impairment) submodel → concentration-time profiles

Monte Carlo population simulation to characterize pharmacokinetic parameter and exposure variability for special population dose adjustments | Monte Carlo population sampling across physiological and clearance parameters in PBPK models → exposure distributions and dose adjustment recommendations

Population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) estimation pipeline with NONMEM primary execution and automatic nlmixr2 (R) fallback when NONMEM is unavailable. BYOL (Bring Your Own License) pattern: -- If NONMEM_HOME and NONMEM_LICENSE_FILE are set → run NONMEM nmfe75/nmfe74 -- Otherwise → fall back to nlmixr2 open-source R implementation Pipeline Steps: 1. -- Validate NONMEM-format dataset structure (ID, TIME, DV, etc.) 2. NONMEM_CTL_GENERATE -- Generate NO
Validate SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) | validation, parsing, and standardization of molecular SMILES input files with paired compound identifiers → validated SMILES dataset

RDKit RECAP decomposition into scaffold and R-groups | retrosynthetic chemical fragmentation of SMILES compounds using RDKit RECAP cleavage rules into core scaffolds and R-groups → decomposed fragments table

mmpdb analysis to calculate property deltas for fragment swaps | matched molecular pair indexing and transformation calculation using mmpdb on fragmented compounds → matched molecular pair database and property delta distribution table

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility (SA) score | multi-parameter scaffold evaluation and prioritization based on occurrence frequency, drug-likeness metrics, and synthetic accessibility (SA) scoring → prioritized candidate scaffold ranking report

Validate expression matrix and clinical metadata alignment, integrity, and sample identifiers | data validation, sample matching, and quality checks on a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix and clinical metadata table → verified expression matrix and sample metadata

Perform voom transformation, fit linear models with clinical covariates, run eBayes moderation, and generate topTable with logFC and adj.P.Val | differential gene expression testing using limma-voom with linear modeling adjusting for covariates and empirical Bayes moderation → differential expression statistics table with logFC and adjusted p-values

Perform GSVA or ssGSEA signature scoring using MSigDB hallmark gene sets (50 gene sets) to identify top enriched pathways per clinical group | single-sample pathway enrichment scoring using GSVA or ssGSEA against the 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets on normalized expression data → sample-level pathway score matrix and group-wise enrichment rankings
